tasks.short: Take the health questions, discuss goals and limits, test the client, write and check the programme, send it to the client and review progress.

steps.what: Trainer goes through the health and goals questions on a paper form at intake
Trainer discusses goals, needs and physical conditions with the client
Trainer tests the client's strength, mobility and fitness
Trainer writes a suitable training program in a spreadsheet to meet special requirements
Trainer prints or e-mails the programme to the client
Trainer reviews progress with the client and adjusts the programme

tasks.design: Clients fill in the health and goals questionnaire online in the gym's member app ({OTHER}) before the intake, so the trainer reviews answers instead of reading out questions. The trainer builds the programme from templates and the gym's exercise library in the app and checks it; once the trainer marks it final, the app sends it to the client. Talking, testing and progress reviews stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Intake forms were paper and programmes were built in spreadsheets from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Gym member apps hold questionnaires, exercise libraries and programmes.
tasks.still_hard: Health answers are special-category data; templates must not replace adapting to the person.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing how a client really moves and what they are afraid of.

reach.task: Hand over clients to the gym
reach.learn: Whether shared programmes in the app ease handovers.

evidence.claim: Gym member apps hold health questionnaires, exercise libraries and programmes.
Health answers are special-category data; a tool that holds them needs a processor contract.

assumptions: Boundary: from intake to the first progress review; nutrition advice is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire filled in by the client; exercise library and templates kept by the gym manager; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Talking, testing and reviews do not change.
Manager time is outside the trainer's savings.
research_questions: Do clients stick to programmes they receive in the app?

approvals.approved_version: The programme as marked final by the trainer in s4; any change is sent only after a new mark.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Clients with complex conditions still need programmes built from scratch.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch and cue intensity, explain exertion zones, check participants' heart rate and tick attendance.

steps.what: Trainer watches participants and cues them to keep exertion levels up or down
Trainer explains heart-rate zones and perceived exertion to maximize benefits from exercise routines
Trainer asks participants their heart rate or has them take their pulse
Trainer ticks attendance on a paper class list

tasks.design: Participants who opt in wear a heart-rate strap, and a screen in the studio shows each person's zone, so the trainer reads it at a glance instead of asking each participant during the class. Attendance is recorded by the members' check-in scan in the gym's member system ({OTHER}); cueing and explaining stay with the trainer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Heart rates were asked out loud and attendance ticked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Studio heart-rate displays and check-in scans are common in gyms.
tasks.still_hard: Heart rate is health data; participants must opt in and the screen must show first names only.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the participant who is pushing too hard before the screen does.

reach.learn: Whether check-in data show which classes fill.

evidence.claim: Studio heart-rate displays show each participant's zone from a chest strap.
Heart-rate data are health data; collect them only with explicit opt-in.

assumptions: Boundary: one class from start to attendance; class planning is outside.
Input contract: straps paired by members who opt in; check-in scanner run by the front desk; fallback is asking and paper.
Cueing and explaining do not change.
Heart-rate data are not stored after the class.
unknowns: Share of participants who would opt in.
research_questions: Do participants spend more time in their target zone?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is coaching in the room.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate equipment, watch the client try it and correct form, and give machine settings in writing.

steps.what: Trainer demonstrates use of training equipment such as weights and trampolines
Trainer watches the client try the equipment and corrects form
Trainer writes machine settings and cues on a card for the client

tasks.design: Each machine carries a code that opens a short video and the standard cues in the gym's member app ({OTHER}), and the trainer only notes the client's personal settings there. Demonstrating and correcting form stay fully with the trainer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Settings and cues were written on cards that got lost.
tasks.enabler_now: Gym apps can link machine codes to videos and personal settings.
tasks.still_hard: Videos do not see bad form; correction needs the trainer.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the rounded back before it becomes an injury.

reach.learn: Whether machine codes cut repeat questions.

evidence.claim: Gym apps link machine codes to instruction videos and members' settings.
Teaching equipment use touches no high-risk AI area; no AI is used.

assumptions: Boundary: from demonstration to settings noted; programme design is outside.
Input contract: videos and cues per machine made by the gym manager; fallback is cards.
Demonstrating and correcting do not change.
Manager time is outside the trainer's savings.
research_questions: Do members ask fewer machine questions?

incremental.description: Trainer enters clients' settings in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is demonstration in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain rules to new members, correct unsafe use on the floor, check signed declarations, check acceptance at entry and write incident reports.

steps.what: Trainer explains safety rules and regulations to new members
Trainer walks the floor and enforces safe use of exercise equipment
Trainer files the paper health declaration and signed house rules
Trainer checks the paper file when unsure whether a member signed the rules
Trainer writes incident reports on paper

tasks.design: Members accept the house rules and fill in the health declaration online when they join the gym's member system ({OTHER}), and the check-in scan admits only members who have accepted. Incident reports use a short form in the same system; explaining rules and correcting unsafe use stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Declarations and rules were signed on paper and filed by staff.
tasks.enabler_now: Gym member systems take online sign-ups and control check-in.
tasks.still_hard: Accepting rules online is not understanding them; safety is enforced on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a member before a dropped weight hurts someone.

reach.learn: Whether form reports show risky equipment.

evidence.claim: Gym member systems take online sign-ups with rule acceptance and control check-in.
Health declarations are special-category data; keep them with restricted access.

assumptions: Boundary: from new member to incident reported; insurance claims are outside.
Input contract: house rules and declaration form set by the gym manager; check-in rules configured by the front desk lead; fallback is paper.
Explaining and enforcing on the floor do not change.
Manager time is outside the trainer's savings.
research_questions: Do incident reports become more complete with a form?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is on the floor.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fitness trainer keeps testing, coaching and safety on the floor; paper forms, lists and cards go.
role.ambitious_version: A trainer who spends every paid minute coaching people, not filling in forms.

job.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
